questions.prompt: Big blind versus button, you have a set on A72 rainbow. The button bets small. Best default?

choices.text: Raise. A set wants a bigger pot, even on a dry board.
Only call and never raise a set
Donk the next street for the minimum no matter what

questions.explanation: Slow-playing a set on a dry board lets the button check back the turn and realize equity for free.

questions.prompt: Big blind versus button, you have bottom pair on As Kd 4c and face a pot-size bet. Best default?

choices.text: Fold. Bottom pair does not beat a real value range and has little equity.
Raise small and call a jam

questions.explanation: Out of position, weak pairs against a large bet are folds, not hero calls.

questions.prompt: Big blind, you called a button open and flopped a nut flush draw on a dry-ish two-tone board. Facing a small bet, a sound continue is…

choices.text: Call or raise. You have nine outs to the nuts plus fold equity if you raise.
Call and stack off if you miss

questions.explanation: Nine outs is enough to continue against a small bet. Missing later is a new decision.

questions.prompt: You are the preflop raiser out of position, heads-up, on a dry board. A check is…

choices.text: Allowed. You can check-call, check-raise, or check-fold. Betting is common but not mandatory.

questions.explanation: Out of position, checking a dry board with a medium hand controls the pot.
